title: High ideal-power product of a coherent module has no ideal-power torsion
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I$ ideal-sheaf data [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $H$ a coherent quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $U$ an open subset with $V(I)=X\setminus U$. Write $P_n,j_n$ for the recursive powers and $I^kH$ for the multiplication image [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. There is $k\in\mathbb N$ such that $P=I^kH$ is quasi-coherent, its canonical inclusion $j:P\to H$ is mono and bijective on $U$-sections, and for every $n,W,x\in P(W)$, if $j_{n,V}(b)x|_V=0$ for every $V\subseteq W$ and $b\in P_n(V)$, then $x=0$.

source.place: Second paragraph of Tag 01YB; Tags 01Y8 and 01YA.

proof.text: Obtain a stabilized annihilator a:T -> H and an exponent r killing its ideal product. Apply the uniform intersection bound to get k with I^k H intersect T contained in I^r T=0. Define P and j as the existing multiplication image and inclusion.

The ideal-data recursive-power comparison gives quasi-coherence of the kth power; tensor quasi-coherence and the image comparison give quasi-coherence of P. Its inclusion is mono as an image inclusion.

The ideal module is finite type. Identify the support complement with a subset of the surjective-stalk open furnished by the power-complement theorem. Lift the unit section through the kth power inclusion on U. The image-factorization applied to its tensor with any section of H lifts that section through j. Monicity gives injectivity.

Naturality and linearity send a locally annihilated section x of P to a locally annihilated section j(x) of H. It lies in T by the stabilized-annihilator clause and in I^k H by construction. The intersection bound puts it in the range of the zero morphism I^r T -> H, so j(x)=0. Sectionwise injectivity of j gives x=0.

proof_origin.place: Original second-paragraph argument, with explicit tensor image lift over the complement; general Artin-Rees equality replaced by the proved uniform intersection inclusion.
